sentences.text:
Rajib Narayan Mukherjee vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on
1 April, 2026
01.04.2026 Sl. No.15.
D/L. Mithun.
Ct.No.29.
Crr/488/2025 Rajib Narayan Mukherjee Vs. The State of West Bengal & Anr.
Mr. Shataroop Purakayastha, Mr. Abhishek Chakraborty, Ms. R. Mazumder ...for the petitioners

The
petitioner herein has assailed the judgment and order dated 6th November, 2024 passed in
Criminal Appeal No.3 of 2023 as well as Criminal cross Appeal No.5 of 2023 whereby the Court
below has acquitted the opposite party no.2 from the charges framed under Sections 420/471 of the
Indian Penal Code and thereby dismissed the appeal.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner/complainant submits that a case under Sections 420/471 IPC was levelled against the opposite party herein being Kaliagaung Police Station Case No.55 dated 11.04.2003 and the charge-sheet was submitted on 15.09.2003.

At the first instance, the Trial Court delivered a judgment on 25.07.2017 whereby the Trial Court acquitted the opposite party no.2 from the allegation of committing offence punishable under Sections 420/471 of the Indian Penal Code.

The complainant/petitioner herein preferred an appeal before the Appellate Court and the Appellate Court by its judgment and order dated 24th February, 2020 directed the Trial Court for conducting re-trial of T.R. No.386 of 2006.
After conducting re-trial, the Trial Court by a judgment and order dated 25th January, 2023 convicted the opposite party no.2 herein under Sections 420/471 of the IPC.

Being aggrieved by the said judgment of conviction, the opposite party no.2 herein preferred a criminal appeal being aforesaid appeal no.3 of 2023 and petitioner preferred cross appeal against awarding lesser punishment being Criminal Appeal no.5 of 2023.
By the impugned judgment dated 06.11.2024, the Court below has acquitted the opposite party no.2 from all charges and thereby disposed of both the appeals.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment of acquittal, learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that learned Sessions Judge failed to apply his mind while the order of acquittal was recorded.
He erroneously held that the department checked all documents but did not detect anything wrong with the opposite party no.2.

The Court below failed to consider the evidence of P.W,10 who is the employee of Ranchi University and had deposed that the University did not provide any diploma in library science whether in 1979 or at any other point of time as claimed by opposite party no.2.

In fact, the certificate produced by opposite party no.2, claimed to have been issued by the Ranchi Rajib Narayan Mukherjee vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170707311/
1 University, was a fake and false document.

sentences.text: Therefore, allegation under Sections 420/471 of the Indian Penal Code has been clearly proved in the present context against the opposite party no.2.
Having heard learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner, the application is admitted.

Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of application upon the State through the office of Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon opposite party no.2 through speed post intimating next date of hearing and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.
Let the matter be listed in the Monthly List of June, 2026.
Parties to act on a server copy of this order duly collected from the official website of the Hon'ble High Court, Calcutta.
( Dr. Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J. )
